title: private-deploy-networking-debug-notes
content:
Notes / breadcrumbs from debugging a customer's Private deployment networking failure (VPC peering + DNS + TLS + egress). Informal, rough. For handoff to SRE/solutions engineering.

Summary:
- Customer reported service-to-controlplane connectivity failures in private deployment: API calls from customer VPC to Redwood control plane intermittently fail (timeouts / TLS handshake errors).
- Affects model load + heartbeat checks. Symptoms started after initial VPC peering + private hosted zone association work.
- Tentative root causes under investigation: (1) incorrect DNS resolution (private hosted zone not associated / resolvable), (2) asymmetric routing / missing route for peering, (3) TLS termination mismatch (SNI/ALPN or missing intermediate CA), (4) egress path hitting corporate proxy dropping TLS.

Timeline / what I tried (chronological):
- 2026-03-03 09:10 — initial report from customer via SolutionsEng Slack.
- 2026-03-03 09:25 — obtained customer VPC ids, peering id (pcx-0a1b2c3d4e), and private hosted zone id (ZPHST-EXAMPLE).
- 2026-03-03 09:35 — sanity checks from my laptop (connected to engineering VPN that has route to customer staging VPC via our transit):
  - dig +noall +answer controlplane.internal.example.com @10.0.0.2  # customer Route53 resolver IP
    -> (no answers)
  - dig +short controlplane.internal.example.com  # allowed to hit system resolver
    ->  (empty)
  - traceroute -n -w 2 controlplane.internal.example.com  # host unreachable / stops at 10.0.128.1 (transit)

- 2026-03-03 10:00 — ran AWS CLI checks (from our account where peering was created):
  - aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --vpc-peering-connection-ids pcx-0a1b2c3d4e --query 'VpcPeeringConnections[0].Status.Code'
    -> "active"
  - aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=private-deploy-* --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'
    -> routes listed but I noticed no explicit route for peer cidr 10.1.0.0/16 in the controlplane-route-table for some subnets (possible missing propagation).

- 2026-03-03 10:20 — Verified customer side: (asked customer to run):
  - aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-123cust" --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'
    -> their route-table for private subnets had route to pcx-0a1b2c3d4e for our controlplane CIDR 10.2.0.0/16
  - aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --vpc-peering-connection-ids pcx-0a1b2c3d4e --query 'VpcPeeringConnections[0].AccepterVpcInfo.CidrBlock'
    -> "10.2.0.0/16"
  - Confirmed peering state active on their end.

- 2026-03-03 10:40 — DNS investigation (private hosted zone / resolver):
  - Observed that controlplane hostname is in a Route53 private hosted zone (ZPHST-EXAMPLE). Private hosted zones only resolve within associated VPCs.
  - Customer confirmed they associated their VPC with the private hosted zone, but association status in our account shows not associated (or associated to different VPC id).
  - Commands run (customer terminal):
    * aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZPHST-EXAMPLE --query 'VPCs'
      -> returned only VPC: vpc-999-other (not the new customer VPC).
  - Hypothesis: hosted zone association didn't complete / associated to wrong VPC. This would cause DNS failures (dig returns nothing).

- 2026-03-03 11:05 — TLS checks (when DNS forced to IP):
  - Asked customer to curl the controlplane IP directly: curl -v https://10.2.45.12:443/health --resolve controlplane.internal.example.com:443:10.2.45.12
    -> curl output: TLS handshake error: "sslv3 alert handshake failure" and sometimes "SSL: certificate subject name mismatch"
  - openssl s_client -connect 10.2.45.12:443 -servername controlplane.internal.example.com
    -> Certificate presented: CN=controlplane.redwood-inference.com, SANs include controlplane.redwood-inference.com but NOT controlplane.internal.example.com. Chain shows intermediate signed by Redwood-CA-2024.
  - Hypothesis: customer is resolving to internal ip where TLS cert has public name; our service expects SNI controlplane.redwood-inference.com. We can either issue certs with internal names or require curl with correct SNI. But certificate mismatch alone shouldn't cause all failures. The "handshake failure" suggests client or middlebox actively terminating.

- 2026-03-03 11:45 — egress/proxy / corporate firewall check:
  - Asked customer to run tcpdump on the host attempting connection: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.45.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/t.pcap
    -> capture shows SYN -> SYN,ACK -> ACK then small TLS ClientHello then immediate RST from gateway (10.1.0.1) within 200ms.
  - Hypothesis: a network appliance (corporate proxy/NGFW) is inspecting TLS and resetting connections that don't match expected SNI or certificate policy. Could also be MTU/path-MTU issue but RST points to filtering.

- 2026-03-03 12:10 — asymmetric routing check:
  - From controlplane side, ran tcpdump on endpoint (10.2.45.12): saw incoming SYN then server replies with SYN,ACK but packets from server go out via transit-gateway to different ENI (10.3.x.x) with no return route to customer VPC -> manifests as RST at some hop.
  - Route tables show one subnet with default route to NAT / shared TGW; missing explicit peering route for customer cidr.
  - Hypothesis: controlplane endpoint chosen an ENI in a subnet that doesn't have correct route to peering. Could be a placement issue or route-table misconfiguration on our side.

- 2026-03-03 13:00 — quick mitigation experiments:
  - Manually added route to controlplane-subnet route-table: Destination = 10.1.0.0/16 -> Target = pcx-0a1b2c3d4e (provisionally). After propagation, customer reports improved connectivity for ~30 minutes, then failures resumed.
  - Rolled back change (to avoid unintended routing in prod) — need proper plan to update all relevant route-tables and ensure idempotent terraform.

Open hypotheses (ranked):
1) DNS not actually associated to the customer's VPC (private hosted zone association mismatch). This explains initial "no answer" on dig. Fix: associate hosted zone to customer VPC (or use Route53 resolver rules / inbound endpoints). Owner: infra-ops / Sean.
2) Asymmetric routing on our controlplane side: some controlplane ENIs/subnets lack route to peering CIDR -> RSTs from intermediate devices. Fix: ensure route-tables for all endpoint subnets have explicit route to peering CIDR or force endpoint into subnets with correct routes. Owner: network-team / Maya.
3) Corporate proxy / NGFW on customer path is active and performing TLS inspection, resetting connections when SNI/cert don't match expected policy. Fix: coordinate with customer security to whitelist endpoints or adjust cert/SNI behavior. Owner: SolutionsEng + customer network lead.
4) TLS cert name mismatch causing some clients to drop connection (less likely to trigger immediate RST). Fix: ensure SANs include internal names or require clients to use public SAN via SNI. Owner: certs-team.
5) Overlapping CIDR / route precedence bug (rare) — if customer VPC has overlapping ranges we might be routing to wrong peer. Fix: verify cidrs unique.

What still needs doing / immediate next steps:
- Confirm hosted zone association state in the account that owns the private hosted zone (we saw it associated to vpc-999-other). If wrong, create association to vpc-123cust and wait for DNS propagation. (Owner: Oliver -> infra-ops).
- Full inventory of controlplane ENIs/subnets and corresponding route-tables. Identify any subnet lacking explicit peering route to customer cidr. (Owner: Maya).
- Reproduce RST locally: run tcpdump from both sides at the same time, collect pcap and correlate timestamps. (Owner: Noah).
- Ask customer to temporarily disable TLS/NGFW inspection for the specific controlplane IP or whitelist our controlplane SNI to see if that eliminates resets. (Owner: Priya / customer eng).
- If manual route fix shows improvement, create terraform change with reviewed impact, roll out to all relevant route-tables, and monitor. (Owner: infra-terraform).
- Create a playbook / checklist for future private-hosted-zone + peering onboarding: ensure hosted zone VPC associations, route-table entries in all controlplane subnets, documented SNI/cert expectations, and test scripts (dig, curl --resolve, tcpdump + pcap upload). (Owner: private-deployments).

Useful commands / snippets I used (copy/paste):
- DNS: dig +noall +answer controlplane.internal.example.com @10.0.0.2
- Force resolve with curl: curl -v --resolve controlplane.internal.example.com:443:10.2.45.12 https://controlplane.internal.example.com/health
- OpenSSL TLS inspect: openssl s_client -connect 10.2.45.12:443 -servername controlplane.internal.example.com -showcerts
- AWS peering status: aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --vpc-peering-connection-ids pcx-0a1b2c3d4e --query 'VpcPeeringConnections[0].Status'
- Route tables: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-123cust --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'
- Tcpdump: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.45.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/controlplane-to-cust.pcap
- Server-side capture: sudo tcpdump -i any host 10.1.0.0/16 or port 443 -w /tmp/server-to-cust.pcap

Logs / snippets captured:
- curl output: * Connected to 10.2.45.12 (10.2.45.12) port 443 (#0)
  * ALPN, offering h2
  * TLS 1.3 (IN), Cipher is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
  * TLS alert: handshake failure
  curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure

- tcpdump (client side) excerpt: 
  12:15:03.123456 IP 10.1.23.45.443 > 10.2.45.12.51824: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
  (immediate RST from gateway 10.1.0.1 after ClientHello)

- openssl s_client cert subject: subject=CN = controlplane.redwood-inference.com
  X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
    DNS:controlplane.redwood-inference.com, DNS:api.redwood-inference.com

Notes to self / reminders:
- When customers use private hosted zones + peering, we must validate both sides: VPC association (route53), peering active, and route tables for all endpoint subnets. Missing any one yields intermittent/asymmetric failures.
- Need to document SNI expectations: we require clients to use SNI controlplane.redwood-inference.com. For customers that insist on internal names, consider issuing internal certs or using a TLS passthrough with mTLS.
- Add test harness that runs during onboarding: dig against resolver IP, curl --resolve to IP, simple TLS cert check (openssl s_client), and tcpdump/pcap collection script. Put this in onboarding checklist.

Attachments / artifacts uploaded to incident ticket: pcap files, aws describe outputs, screenshots of dig/curl. See JIRA-PDEPLOY-987 for links.

If I/O/OOM: ping me (oliver) but hand off to Maya for route fixes and to Sean for hosted zone association.

End.
